title: Smartwatch alert for an irregular rate above 180 bpm leads to a ventricular tachycardia diagnosis, an ICD, and the incidental discovery and resection of a lung adenocarcinoma
summary: A 58-year-old's smartwatch flagged an irregular rate over 180 bpm; NSVT was diagnosed from watch data, an ICD placed, and the post-procedure X-ray found a 28 mm lung adenocarcinoma, resected.
account: Cole, Kar, Nimako and Smelt reported a case in JRSM Open (4 January 2022; event dates not reported). They are of St George's Healthcare NHS Trust (thoracic surgery) and East Surrey Hospital (respiratory medicine) in England's National Health Service (NHS). A previously well 58-year-old non-smoker's smartwatch alerted him that his heart rate was irregular and exceeding 180 beats per minute while he felt nothing. His GP's 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) showed tachycardia without arrhythmia and he was admitted. Inpatient ECGs showed incomplete right bundle branch block and intermittent first-degree AV block but captured no significant arrhythmia. From the smartwatch results, the cardiologist diagnosed non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT) and an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) was inserted. The post-procedure chest X-ray, taken to exclude pneumothorax, incidentally showed a right upper zone abnormality. Computed tomography (CT) found a 28 mm lesion, PET showed FDG-avid nodes, and biopsy showed lepidic adenocarcinoma, staged cT1c N0 M0. He had a video-assisted right upper lobectomy with node dissection and was discharged on day 10. The 35 mm tumor was staged pT2a pN0 M0 with clear margins. The nodes showed sarcoidosis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) found no cardiac sarcoid. The authors call this the first reported case of a smartwatch assisting the diagnosis of both NSVT and lung adenocarcinoma. The watch's brand and model are not stated.
purpose: The watch's heart-rate alert was its intended function. The lung cancer diagnosis was an incidental consequence of the ICD procedure the alert set in motion, outside anything the device was built to do.
system: Smartwatch heart-rate and irregular-rhythm alert (brand and model not stated)
developer: Not stated (the report does not name the device's maker)
location: United Kingdom (authors at St George's Healthcare NHS Trust, London, and East Surrey Hospital, Redhill; the treating hospitals are not named)

ratings.reason: One man received an ICD for ventricular tachycardia and curative resection of a lung adenocarcinoma found at stage pT2a pN0. The authors judge that without the watch the cancer would likely have grown undetected and curative surgery might not have been an option. That counterfactual is their judgment.

ai_role.statement: The watch's alert in an asymptomatic man started the chain. Its stored data were what the cardiologist used to diagnose NSVT when hospital tracings captured nothing. The lung cancer was found by a routine post-ICD X-ray, not by the device. The brand is unknown, so the alerting algorithm cannot be identified. The authors describe smartwatch rhythm monitoring generically as photoplethysmography.

must_hold: The arrhythmia is one the watch records while hospital monitoring misses it

fields.account: Cole, Kar, Nimako and Smelt reported a case in JRSM Open (4 January 2022; event dates not reported). They are of St George's Healthcare NHS Trust (thoracic surgery) and East Surrey Hospital (respiratory medicine) in England's National Health Service (NHS). A previously well 58-year-old non-smoker's smartwatch alerted him that his heart rate was irregular and exceeding 180 beats per minute while he felt nothing. His GP's 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) showed tachycardia without arrhythmia and he was admitted. Inpatient ECGs showed incomplete right bundle branch block and intermittent first-degree AV block but captured no significant arrhythmia. From the smartwatch results, the cardiologist diagnosed non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT) and an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) was inserted. The post-procedure chest X-ray, taken to exclude pneumothorax, incidentally showed a right upper zone abnormality. Computed tomography (CT) found a 28 mm lesion, PET showed FDG-avid nodes, and biopsy showed lepidic adenocarcinoma, staged cT1c N0 M0. He had a video-assisted right upper lobectomy with node dissection and was discharged on day 10. The 35 mm tumor was staged pT2a pN0 M0 with clear margins. The nodes showed sarcoidosis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) found no cardiac sarcoid. The authors call this the first reported case of a smartwatch assisting the diagnosis of both NSVT and lung adenocarcinoma. The watch's brand and model are not stated.
